title: Mailchimp vs Brevo vs Kit: Which Email Marketing Platform Fits a Small Business in 2026?
excerpt: Compare Mailchimp, Brevo and Kit by pricing model, free limits, automation and audience fit. Choose an email platform without paying for features your business will not use.
html:
Mailchimp, Brevo and Kit can all send newsletters, but they are built around different kinds of businesses. Mailchimp is a broad marketing platform with contact-based plan limits. Brevo combines email with CRM and other channels, and its plans are structured around sending volume and contact storage. Kit is designed for creators who build an audience through newsletters, forms and digital products.

That difference matters more than a long feature checklist. A business with a large contact database but modest sending needs can face a very different bill from a creator who sends frequent broadcasts to active subscribers. The right choice depends on how your list grows, how often you email it and whether you need automated customer journeys.

Pricing note: This comparison uses the vendors' public US-dollar pricing and help pages checked on November 8, 2026. Prices are starting points, not quotes for every list size. Currency, tax, billing term, location, add-ons and contact or send tier can change the amount you pay.

Quick verdict

  • Choose Mailchimp if you want a broad email-marketing suite, a large integration ecosystem and familiar campaign, audience and reporting tools. Check the contact tier and send allowance before importing a large list.
  • Choose Brevo if you send based on campaign volume, need to store a sizeable contact database, or want email alongside basic sales and multichannel tools. Check which automation features are included at your chosen tier.
  • Choose Kit if your business is built around a newsletter, creator audience, digital products or paid subscriptions. Its free subscriber allowance is generous, but visual automations and email sequences require a paid plan.

There is no universal winner. A platform that is inexpensive for a newsletter creator may be a poor fit for an ecommerce team that needs customer journeys, purchase events and multiple staff accounts.

Mailchimp vs Brevo vs Kit at a glance

PlatformFree-plan headlinePublished paid starting pointMain pricing driverBest-fit use case
Mailchimp250 contacts; 500 sends per month, with a 250-per-day capEssentials from $13/month; Standard from $20/monthContact tier, plan and monthly send allowanceSmall businesses wanting a broad marketing suite and integrations
Brevo300 sends per day; storage for up to 100,000 contacts; limited automationStarter from $9/month; Standard from $18/monthMonthly email volume and the associated contact-storage tierBusinesses balancing list size, send volume and multichannel needs
KitUp to 10,000 active subscribers and unlimited broadcastsCreator from $39/month; Pro from $79/month at the 1,000-subscriber starting tierActive subscriber tier and plan levelNewsletter writers, educators, coaches and digital-product creators

Mailchimp's free plan is deliberately small: the vendor lists one seat, one audience and a maximum of 250 contacts, with sending paused if a contact or send limit is exceeded. Its pricing page lists Essentials from $13 and Standard from $20 per month; actual charges rise with the selected contact tier. Mailchimp's published monthly send multipliers are 10 times the contact count for Essentials, 12 times for Standard and 15 times for Premium.

Brevo's free plan allows 300 sends per day and stores up to 100,000 contacts, but those stored contacts should not be confused with unlimited free automation. Brevo lists multi-channel marketing automation for up to 2,000 contacts on Free. Starter begins at $9 per month for a 5,000-send tier with up to 500 stored contacts; higher tiers pair larger send volumes with larger contact allowances. Standard starts at $18 and adds marketing automation for unlimited contacts, A/B testing and advanced reporting.

Kit's free Newsletter plan supports up to 10,000 active subscribers and unlimited email broadcasts. It does not include visual automations or email sequences. Kit's help centre lists Creator at $39 per month and Pro at $79 per month for up to 1,000 subscribers; annual billing is advertised as two months free. Paid prices scale with subscriber count.

1. Mailchimp: the broad marketing-suite option

Mailchimp makes sense when email is one part of a wider marketing operation. Its platform combines campaigns, audience management, forms, reporting and a large integration catalogue. That can be useful for a small retailer, service business or marketing team that wants one familiar place to manage several campaign types.

Where Mailchimp is strongest

  • Integrations: Mailchimp lists more than 300 integrations, which can reduce manual work when connecting ecommerce, forms, analytics and customer systems.
  • Campaign tooling: Paid plans add scheduling, templates, testing and reporting options. Standard adds more advanced automation and optimisation features than Essentials.
  • Team structure: The published plan comparison shows more seats and audiences as you move up the tiers, which can matter when marketing work is shared.
  • Familiar ecosystem: Businesses already using connected tools may prefer extending an existing Mailchimp setup over rebuilding campaign processes elsewhere.

Where to be careful

The free plan is now a small testing tier, not a long-term newsletter plan for a growing business. At 250 contacts and 500 monthly sends, a list can outgrow it quickly. Paid pricing is contact-based, and each plan has a send multiplier. If your contact count rises, your monthly cost can rise even when you do not send more campaigns.

Do not compare the $13 Essentials starting price with a competitor's price for a much larger list. Select your expected contact count, monthly send volume, number of users and required automation steps in Mailchimp's calculator before budgeting. Also review overage rules: Mailchimp says charges can apply when contact or send limits are exceeded.

2. Brevo: a volume-led option with CRM and multichannel tools

Brevo is worth evaluating when the number of messages you send is a better cost driver than the number of people stored in your database. Its plans pair monthly send volume with contact-storage tiers. That structure can suit a business that maintains a larger customer database but sends campaigns selectively.

Where Brevo is strongest

  • Large free contact storage: The Free plan can store up to 100,000 contacts, while daily sending is capped at 300 emails. Storage capacity is not the same as permission to email everyone on that list.
  • Volume tiers: Starter and Standard tiers are tied to monthly email sends and contact storage. Brevo's published guide lists 5,000 sends with up to 500 contacts, 10,000 with up to 1,500, and 15,000 with up to 2,500 on the entry tiers.
  • Sales features: Brevo includes free sales features and positions itself as a wider customer-relationship platform, not only a newsletter sender.
  • Multichannel extensions: SMS and WhatsApp options can be added where available and appropriate, but these can carry separate eligibility, credit and pricing conditions.

Where to be careful

Brevo's free plan has a daily send cap, so a large campaign may need to be split across days or moved to a paid tier. Some features that look similar in a plan comparison are not included at every level. For example, the Standard plan adds unlimited-contact marketing automation, A/B testing and advanced analytics; Free automation is limited to 2,000 contacts.

Before choosing Brevo, calculate both your stored contacts and your monthly sends. A business with 2,000 contacts that sends four campaigns to the whole list needs roughly 8,000 campaign sends in a normal month, before welcome emails, receipts or other messages are counted. Use the current pricing calculator to select a tier that covers the actual workload.

3. Kit: built for newsletter-led businesses and creators

Kit is a different kind of choice. It is designed around creators who publish regularly, collect subscribers through forms and landing pages, and earn from products, memberships or newsletters. It is less of an all-purpose CRM than a platform for owning and monetising an audience.

Where Kit is strongest

  • Generous free audience allowance: The free plan supports up to 10,000 active subscribers and unlimited broadcasts, which is attractive for a creator who mainly sends newsletters.
  • Audience tools: Forms, landing pages, tagging and segmentation help creators organise readers by interests and signup source.
  • Creator commerce: Kit supports digital products and recurring subscriptions, so a creator can connect email with a paid newsletter or product offer.
  • Automation on paid plans: Creator adds visual automations and email sequences. Pro adds deeper analytics, collaboration and deliverability reporting.

Where to be careful

The free plan is not a substitute for a full automation platform. Kit's help centre says visual automations, email sequences and RSS campaigns are paid-plan features. If your business depends on multi-step onboarding, abandoned-cart flows or customer lifecycle journeys, include the Creator subscription in your budget from the beginning.

Kit's paid starting prices are based on a 1,000-subscriber tier and scale with the audience. Annual billing can reduce the effective monthly price, but check the renewal amount and the exact subscriber tier before paying. A limited-time promotion on a pricing page should not be treated as the permanent renewal price.

Which pricing model will cost less for your list?

Think about the unit each vendor charges for, not only the headline price.

  • Mailchimp: Model your highest expected contact tier and the plan's monthly send multiplier. This is straightforward when the list is stable, but can become expensive if your stored audience grows faster than your sending needs.
  • Brevo: Estimate monthly sends and the contact-storage tier together. It can be attractive when you store many contacts but send selectively. The daily cap on Free and the feature gates between Starter and Standard still matter.
  • Kit: Estimate active subscribers and decide whether the free plan's broadcast-only workflow is enough. If you need automated sequences, budget for Creator or Pro rather than assuming the 10,000-subscriber free tier includes every feature.

For a practical example, imagine a creator with 4,000 active readers who sends one newsletter every week. Kit Free may cover the broadcast requirement while the list stays under 10,000, provided the creator does not need visual automations or sequences. A small retailer with 4,000 stored customer records and a few targeted campaigns may prefer to compare Brevo's volume tiers. A business that depends on a broad ecommerce integration stack may prefer Mailchimp even if its price is higher.

These are workload examples, not price quotes. Before subscribing, add up campaign sends, triggered emails, staff seats, add-ons, taxes, migration effort and any overage charges. Also check how each vendor treats unsubscribed, inactive or duplicate records in its billing calculations.

Feature fit: use your workflow to choose

If your main requirement is…Start by evaluatingWhy
Broad integrations and campaign reportingMailchimpIt offers a wider marketing-suite approach and a large integration catalogue.
Large stored list with controlled sending volumeBrevoIts plan tiers combine monthly sends with contact storage.
Newsletter publishing and creator productsKitIts free plan and creator-focused commerce tools are designed for that model.
Multi-step automation for a growing businessCompare Brevo Standard, Mailchimp Standard and Kit CreatorEach gates automation differently; map the exact triggers and branches you need.
Multiple staff members and approval workflowsCompare paid team limits before choosingSeat counts and collaboration features vary by tier.

If your email platform needs to connect to a CRM, compare the whole customer workflow rather than buying a standalone newsletter tool in isolation. Our HubSpot vs Pipedrive vs Zoho CRM comparison explains how CRM pricing and sales-seat needs can change the software decision. If you want to connect signups, sales updates and campaign reporting, our Zapier vs Make automation-cost guide can help estimate the extra workflow layer. For a broader view of a small-business software stack, see our practical AI tools guide.

Deliverability and setup matter more than a template gallery

No email platform can guarantee that every campaign reaches the inbox. Sender reputation, recipient engagement, list quality, authentication and message content all influence delivery. A polished template does not compensate for an old list or missing domain authentication.

  1. Authenticate your sending domain. Follow the vendor's current setup instructions for SPF and DKIM, and publish a DMARC policy that fits your organisation's mail setup. Do not copy DNS records from an unrelated domain.
  2. Import only contacts you are allowed to email. Keep the source, date and method of consent. Do not assume that a purchased, scraped or publicly visible address is automatically eligible for marketing.
  3. Start with a small, relevant segment. Send to recent, engaged subscribers first. Remove hard bounces and suppress unsubscribed contacts.
  4. Test the whole journey. Check the signup form, confirmation message, welcome email, links, mobile rendering and unsubscribe flow before launching a campaign.
  5. Measure useful outcomes. Track clicks, replies, purchases, qualified leads and unsubscribes. Treat open rates carefully because privacy features and mail clients can distort open tracking.
  6. Keep an export and recovery plan. Know how to export contacts, consent records, segments, templates and automation logic before you depend on a platform.

Consent and compliance for US, UK, Canadian and Australian audiences

Email marketing rules differ by sender, recipient type and message. A platform's compliance features do not make your campaign automatically lawful. This is a practical orientation, not legal advice; review the rules that apply to your business and get qualified advice where needed.

  • United States: The FTC's CAN-SPAM guidance requires accurate sender information, non-deceptive subject lines, a valid physical postal address and a clear way to opt out. Opt-out requests must be honoured within 10 business days. The rules also apply to commercial business-to-business email.
  • Canada: CASL generally requires prior express or qualifying implied consent, sender identification and contact information, and a working unsubscribe mechanism. The CRTC says unsubscribe requests must be processed within 10 business days. Keep evidence of the consent basis.
  • United Kingdom: Under PECR, unsolicited marketing email to individual subscribers generally needs consent unless a specific soft opt-in applies. Different rules can apply to corporate subscribers, but senders must not hide their identity and must provide a valid contact address for opt-outs.
  • Australia: The ACMA says commercial messages need consent, must identify the sender and include contact details, and must make unsubscribing easy. The Spam Act requires unsubscribe requests to be actioned within five working days.

Use the platform's consent fields, suppression lists and unsubscribe tools, but keep your own records of when and how each person subscribed. Do not upload a list just because the software accepts the CSV.

A seven-step buying checklist

  1. Write down your current number of marketable contacts and expected growth over the next year.
  2. Estimate monthly campaign sends plus triggered messages such as welcome, order and service emails.
  3. List the automations you actually need: a welcome sequence, lead follow-up, post-purchase education or re-engagement.
  4. Confirm how many staff need access and whether approval or collaborative editing is required.
  5. Check integrations with your website, CRM, ecommerce platform and analytics tools.
  6. Compare the total price at your expected contact and send tier, including taxes, add-ons and annual renewal.
  7. Run a small pilot, test consent and unsubscribe handling, and export a backup before migrating your full list.

Frequently asked questions

Which is the cheapest email marketing platform?

There is no single cheapest option for every business. Kit has a free plan for up to 10,000 active subscribers if broadcasts are enough. Brevo's free plan has a 300-per-day send cap and large contact storage. Mailchimp's free plan is limited to 250 contacts and 500 monthly sends. Paid costs depend on the list, send volume and features you need.

Is Brevo better than Mailchimp for a small business?

Brevo can be a better fit when you store many contacts but send fewer campaigns, or when its sales and multichannel features match your workflow. Mailchimp can be a better fit when you value its integration ecosystem and broader marketing tools. Compare the same contact count, monthly sends and automation requirements in both calculators.

Is Kit suitable for a normal service business?

It can work if the main job is publishing a newsletter, collecting subscribers and selling services or digital products to an audience. If you need sales pipelines, customer support workflows, ecommerce segmentation or multi-user campaign operations, compare a broader marketing or CRM platform first.

Can I move from one platform to another?

Usually, you can export contacts and import them elsewhere, but forms, templates, tags, automations, suppression records and consent evidence may need careful rebuilding. Do not migrate until you know which data and workflows transfer and have tested a sample export.

Will changing platforms improve inbox placement?

Not automatically. Authentication, sender reputation, list quality, consent, bounce handling and recipient engagement still matter. A new platform can provide better tools, but it cannot guarantee inbox placement.

The bottom line

Mailchimp, Brevo and Kit solve different email-marketing problems. Mailchimp is the broad marketing-suite option, Brevo is worth a close look when send volume and contact storage drive the economics, and Kit is built for creators who make a newsletter part of their business. Start with your audience model and the workflows you need, then compare the real plan tier—not the lowest number on a pricing page.

Pricing and features change. Recheck the linked vendor pages before signing up, especially if you are comparing annual offers, country-specific billing or add-ons.
